text: Theo’s childhood was defined by the quiet intimacy of the rooftop, where he would lie on his back and trace the constellations with a reverence that belied his age. This passion was not merely a pastime but a sacred tether to his late mother, an astrophysicist who had taught him that the night sky was a library of stories waiting to be read. She had encouraged his curiosity, explaining that the fluffy things in the sky rain comes from were not just clouds, but complex systems of water vapor and ice crystals that played a crucial role in the Earth's climate, much like the stars played a role in the cosmos. Her absence left a void that Theo sought to fill by understanding the universe, believing that if he could comprehend the mechanics of the heavens, he might somehow keep her memory alive. This deep-seated need for connection and understanding drove his actions, transforming his stargazing from a simple hobby into a profound quest for meaning and continuity.
